text: You're online, a great offer: "Try Free for 30 Days!" Explore without upfront cost. You just want to check it out.
You click, eager to dive in. But before you start: "Enter your credit card details to begin your free trial."
You immediately wonder why. Is it to verify identity, or prevent multiple sign-ups? These seem like logical reasons.
The true reason is simpler: human inertia. They know once your card is on file, most people won't cancel when the trial ends.
The "free" trial quietly rolls into a paid subscription. You're charged for a service you might not use, because cancelling felt like effort.
Now you see the system. Free trials with card details are less about trying, more about nudging you to stay. Cancel if you don't need it.
